stamp: {"keys":[{"id":"list-holds-what-it-is-not","problem":"The page says it lists the products the site knows but cannot yet explain, yet many of its entries are not products at all: a fee, a fund's label, a gold price benchmark, a role, an event, a grant. A reader cannot trust that the list says what is really missing, and a fee the site does handle elsewhere shows up as unknown, so the whole list reads as unchecked.","where":"the cards of the list under the title and subtitle at the top (for example the cards of an exchange fee, a gold price, a rating company, a debt settlement)","kind":"general"},{"id":"bare-code","problem":"Where a card says what blocks it, some lines show only an internal code (letters and a number) instead of the question in words, so the reader cannot tell what is still open.","where":"the 'what blocks it' line of a few cards, beside the words 'open question' or 'set on'","kind":"general"},{"id":"fragment-no-noun","problem":"Lines under 'what was closed' read as fragments, a struck-out date followed by a bare number and a link, with no noun saying what the number counts or what was closed, so they mean nothing to a reader.","where":"the 'what was closed' lines of the open cards","kind":"general"},{"id":"source-names-not-for-reader","problem":"Some source lines name the source in English or as a copy (a wiki copy, a 'hosted copy', an English office name inside the Hebrew page) and still label it a primary source, which tells a reader neither who the source is nor whether to trust it.","where":"the source line under 'what is known' on a few cards","kind":"general"},{"id":"same-promise-every-card","problem":"Every open card ends with the same long promise of everything that will appear once it is closed (several pages and features named), the same words on each, more than the reader can believe will happen for each entry.","where":"the line starting 'when it is closed' at the bottom of each open card","kind":"general"}],"liked":[]}

problems.why: Finding 1 says the same thing: the list is headed as products but holds a fee, a price, a rating company and a debt arrangement, which makes the reader doubt the whole list.
Finding 5 complains about unexplained codes like MF-28 and TX2-01 in the coverage boxes, which is the bare internal code problem.
Finding 5 also flags the crossed-out dates as unexplained, a clear part of the person's complaint that the struck-date fragments mean nothing to a reader.
The only finding about source lines (3) says they are tiny and cut off, not that they name English or copied sources mislabelled as primary.
Finding 6 names the same long 'כשייסגר' sentence repeated on every card.

Finding 1 says the 'products' heading is wrong because the list holds a fee, a rating company, a debt arrangement and a price, and that this makes the reader doubt the whole list, which is the person's problem.
Finding 5 complains about unexplained internal codes such as MF-28 and TX2-01 in the cards' status boxes, which matches the bare codes shown instead of the question in words.
Finding 5 also calls the crossed-out dates unexplained, a clear part of the person's complaint that the struck-out-date lines mean nothing to a reader.
No finding is about sources being named in English or as copies while labelled primary; finding 3 only says the source lines are tiny and cut off.
Finding 6 names the same long 'when it is closed' sentence repeated on every card.
